theory: Qualify the degree claim: real zero multiplicities sum to the degree only when the polynomial splits completely into real linear factors; $x^2+1$ is a counterexample to the current unrestricted statement. Likewise, step 1 must not imply that every real polynomial can be completely factorised into real linear factors. In the intro, the zero is the intercept's $x$-coordinate, while the intercept itself is $(\alpha,0)$.
